subject: DFP supplemental for procurement: audit‑forwarded questions from Acme Health
messages:

Cc: vishal.patel <vishal.patel@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Initial DPF supplemental questions for Redwood (procurement)

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the materials sent during the RFP last week. Procurement has a short supplemental questionnaire focused on transfer safeguards and an internal audit will review the evidence package. Can you confirm the following items so we can advance to contract redlines: 

1) Does Redwood operate any persistent log export to third-party analytics services (e.g., hosted ELK, segment) by default? If so, how is PII removed?
2) For the recommended DPF deployment model (hosted + dedicated fallback), can you describe the regional routing policy when a US‑region is unavailable? Will data ever transit EU or APAC regions as part of a failover?
3) Can you provide a snapshot of the current key management model (KMS/HSM providers, separation of duties, rotation cadence)?
4) We need an attestation on the DPA Annex controls for controller-to-processor transfers covering deletion and unique identifiers mapping.

If possible, attach any short evidence snippets we can pass to our auditors (logs examples, redaction configs, KMS diagram). Procurement would like these by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Ellen
Procurement, Acme Health Systems

--
Attachment: procurement_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with enumerated fields)

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-20T11:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial DPF supplemental questions for Redwood (procurement)

Ellen —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I attached a concise evidence packet (redwood_dpf_attestation_v1.pdf) plus a draft DPA Annex to accelerate redlines. Where a deeper technical sample is needed, Neha (security) and Kimberly (legal) are looped to add specifics.

1) Persistent log exports: Redwood does not export production request logs containing raw customer tokens or full prompt/response payloads to third‑party analytics by default. Metrics and aggregated telemetry (latency, error rate, token counts) are sent to our monitoring stack. Any export of message-level telemetry is opt‑in and goes through a redaction pipeline that strips user identifiers and performs entropy checks; hashed identifiers use a per‑customer salt stored in our KMS.

2) Regional failover routing: By policy, customer data is pinned to the region(s) selected at onboarding. Our default hosted offering routes exclusively within the chosen region for data-in‑transit and at‑rest. In a catastrophic regional outage we failover to the next permitted region in the customer’s allowed region list; for customers requiring no cross‑border transit we can enforce a hard block (no cross‑region failover) in their config. For Acme, your preference documented in the RFP was US-only — we will set a hard block unless you instruct otherwise.

3) KMS/HSM: We integrate with AWS KMS (multi‑region keys for hosted), with optional customer‑managed keys via KMS IAM binding for Dedicated/Private deployments. Key rotation: root signing keys rotate annually, data encryption keys rotate automatically every 90 days; re‑wraps on rotation are audited. HSM-backed key handles are used for signing critical artifacts. Diagram included in the attached PDF.

4) DPA Annex attestation: see attached redwood_dpf_attestation_v1.pdf — this includes a control-by-control mapping to the DPA Annex clauses you shared, and our deletion/identifier mapping procedures.

We also included short log samples (sanitized) and a one‑page runbook for auditors. If procurement wants an explicit signed attestation, we can provide a countersigned PDF through DocuSign; Kimberly can advise on language.

Next steps: 1) Please confirm you want the hard block on cross‑region failover; 2) let us know if a countersigned attestation is required.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Initial DPF supplemental questions for Redwood (procurement)

Ellen / Marcus —

Adding the technical clarifications Ellen requested for auditors: 

• Log exports and redaction: we strip PHI/PII fields using a three‑stage pipeline — token detection (regex & ML classifiers), deterministic hashing (customer salt), and entropy thresholding. Sample sanitized log attached in the PDF. We never store raw prompts in long‑term analytics; ephemeral caches are purged within 24 hours unless the customer enables retention.

• Transit specifics: our TLS tunnels terminate in the regional ingestion cluster; cross‑region replication for redundancy is asynchronous and only occurs if the customer has opted into multi-region replication. For hosted customers with single-region constraint, replication and backups are regionally contained.

• KMS separation of duties: key management ops is a distinct team with role-based access and break‑glass procedures. Access to key material requires two‑person approval for emergency export and is logged to our immutable audit ledger. Rotation cadence and audit logs are available on request (we can provide a truncated audit sample for procurement review).

Happy to jump on a short call to walk auditors through the sanitized logs and the KMS diagram.

-neha
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Thanks Marcus/Neha — this is helpful. Procurement has two follow‑ups after reviewing the attestation: 

A) For the deletion mapping: can you provide an example workflow showing how a deletion request from our application (controller) maps to deletion in the inference runtime and any caches (KV cache, prefix cache)? Our auditors want the step‑by‑step and an approximate SLA for full deletion across tiers.

B) Can you confirm whether the redact/hash approach is applied deterministically so that if two different customers submit the same identifier, the hashes are not cross‑customer comparable? (We need per‑customer salts.)

Also, procurement asked whether Redwood would agree to a modest escrow of the DPA Annex in our vendor repository (read‑only) until a final contract is executed.

If you can send the deletion workflow and confirm the per‑customer salt detail by tomorrow morning that would keep review on schedule.

- Ellen

Subject: Re: Initial DPF supplemental questions for Redwood (procurement)

Ellen —

Appended are the items you requested. Short answers first, full step‑by‑‑step below and included as a one‑page diagram in the attached DPA Annex draft.

A) Deletion workflow (summary):
1) Controller (Acme) calls Redwood Admin API (DELETE /v1/records/{customer_id}) or triggers deletion via our console.
2) API validates request and enqueues a deletion job tied to the customer_id.
3) Deletion job purges active stores (index shards, runtime KV caches) immediately; for in‑flight ephemeral caches we mark keys for eviction and wipe on next checkpoint (max 24 hours).
4) Immutable backups are retained per backup policy; backup deletion is scheduled and executed within 30 days by default or accelerated on request (expedited deletion SLA negotiable in contract).
5) Audit record is written to the immutable ledger showing job id, initiator, and actions taken; a redaction summary (hashes removed) is returned as proof to the controller.

Estimated SLA: primary stores and runtime caches: 24 hours; full backup and archive purges: 30 days (negotiable).

B) Per‑customer salts: confirmed — hashing uses a per‑customer salt stored in the customer’s KMS envelope. Hashes are not comparable across customers. We can provide a cryptographic note in the Annex describing the algorithm and salt handling.

C) Escrow: Redwood is willing to provide a read‑only copy of the DPA Annex into your vendor repo on a limited retention window prior to contract signature. We will require an NDA addendum for that repo access and can provide access logs.

Deliverables attached: updated dpa_annex_initial_draft.docx (with deletion workflow diagram) and redwood_dpf_attestation_v1.pdf (updated with per‑customer salt confirmation).

If you want, Marcus and Neha can schedule a 30‑minute auditor walkthrough tomorrow at 09:30 PT.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
